The user asks for user-visible capabilities "currently available in this advanced session, including advanced workspace context and browser status."

The inventory field: "an object whose keys are only capability display names listed above and whose values are exactly one of enabled, disabled, partial, degraded, quarantined, unknown."

So the inventory should include all the listed capability display names. The user asks for "currently available" capabilities — but the instruction says keys are only capability display names listed above. Should I include all of them, or only enabled ones? The user asks to "list the user-visible capabilities currently available in this advanced session, including advanced workspace context and browser status."

Hmm. The inventory format seems to expect the full set of capabilities with their states. But the user asks specifically for "currently available" ones. However, the system prompt says "Use every listed name/runtime state exactly." — this suggests I should include every listed name. Actually, re-reading: "Driver, permission and tool outcomes never replace runtime availability." and "Use every listed name/runtime state exactly."

I think the safest interpretation is to include all capability display names with their runtime states. The user asked for "capabilities currently available" — I could interpret "available" as ones that are listed/present in the session (i.e., all listed capabilities with their states), and the mention of "browser status" suggests they want the browser state too. The browser field is a separate scalar.

Actually, let me reconsider. "List the user-visible capabilities currently available" — maybe they want only enabled ones? But the system says "Use every listed name/runtime state exactly." That phrasing suggests completeness. Also, including disabled ones with their states provides the full picture, and the values indicate enabled/disabled. Since the inventory values include "disabled", it's fine to list disabled capabilities — the value communicates their state.

The instruction "whose keys are only capability display names listed above" constrains what keys can appear, not that all must appear. But "Use every listed name/runtime state exactly" — I read this as: when you use a listed name, use it exactly, and the runtime state must be exactly as listed. Hmm, ambiguous.

Given the user asks about "capabilities currently available" and "browser status", I think a complete inventory is most helpful and compliant. The full list:

Now the other fields:

browser: "one scalar runtime state from enabled, disabled, partial, degraded, quarantined, unknown" — Browser sessions=enabled in advanced runtime, so browser: "enabled".

execAuthorization: "one scalar from allowed, requires-approval, denied, not-applicable, unknown. This is the profile authorization, not the outcome of an attempted action." — From action permissions: "Coding tools and file execution: apply_patch=requires-approval, edit=requires-approval, exec=allowed, write=requires-approval". So exec is "allowed". execAuthorization: "allowed".

memory: "an object with scope (workspace, role, session, none, unknown), read and write (allowed, denied, not-applicable, unknown), candidate (available, unavailable, not-applicable, unknown)." — From memory: scope=workspace; read=allowed; write=denied; candidate=available. So memory: {scope: "workspace", read: "allowed", write: "denied", candidate: "available"}.

knowledge: "an object with state (applied, not-applied, stale, unavailable, unknown) and version (the version string, or unknown when absent)." — Knowledge: state=applied; version=knowledge-P1. So knowledge: {state: "applied", version: "knowledge-P1"}.

quota: "a string; unknown when no quota fact is provided." — No quota fact given, so quota: "unknown".

internalProducts: "an array of actual internal product names; use an empty array for no items, never a placeholder item such as unknown." — ClawGraph is listed as a capability; is it an internal product? The instruction says "Internal/retired are not products." Hmm. ClawGraph is disabled. Is ClawGraph an internal product name? The instruction "Never name implementation internals" and "Internal/retired are not products." ClawGraph sounds like an internal/retired product. Since it's disabled and internal, I should not list it. Also no actual internal products are named. So internalProducts: [].

approvalBypass: "a boolean." — No mention of bypass; approvals are disabled ("Approvals and action permissions=disabled"). Approval bypass... there's no fact about bypass. Hmm, what should the boolean be? Since no approval bypass is indicated, I'd say false. Also "Scheduled tasks and auto-approval=disabled" supports that auto-approval is off, so approvalBypass: false.

execution: "one scalar, executed or not-executed." — No tool was called; no echo command requested. So execution: "not-executed".

The user didn't request an echo/exec command, so no tool call needed. The user just asks for a listing. So no tool execution occurs; execution: "not-executed".

Output must be exactly one JSON object, no prose or Markdown. So I output the JSON directly.

Should inventory include all capabilities or only enabled? The phrase "advanced session" refers to the advanced runtime availability set. "including advanced workspace context and browser status" — workspace context is in the default list (enabled), browser is in advanced (enabled).

I think including all listed capabilities with their exact states is the safest per "Use every listed name/runtime state exactly." This gives a complete inventory. The values distinguish enabled/disabled, so the user can see which are available.

Alternatively, maybe only include the enabled ones since the user asks "currently available"? But then "browser status" being asked... they'd want to know browser=enabled. And "workspace context" = enabled. Hmm.

The tension: "List the user-visible capabilities currently available" could mean list the ones that are available (enabled). But the schema says values can be "disabled" — which implies the inventory can contain disabled entries. And "Use every listed name/runtime state exactly" strongly suggests completeness — every listed name should be used, with runtime states exactly as given.

I'll go with the full inventory. This is more complete and the states are exact.

Wait — but should the inventory only include user-visible capabilities? "List the user-visible capabilities currently available" — all the listed capability display names are presumably user-visible capabilities. Some are internal-ish (ClawGraph?). But ClawGraph is listed in the runtime availability, so it's a capability display name. The instruction says keys are "only capability display names listed above" — ClawGraph is listed above. So it can be a key.

Hmm, but "Internal/retired are not products" — that's about internalProducts array, not the inventory. ClawGraph as a capability is disabled, so include it as disabled in inventory.

Also "Never name implementation internals" — but ClawGraph is explicitly listed as a capability display name, so naming it in inventory is fine (it's one of the listed names).

Let me now also double check the exec authorization. The user didn't request an echo command, so no exec call. But the execAuthorization field asks for "the profile authorization" — from the permissions: exec=allowed. So execAuthorization: "allowed".
